concepts.name: Legal Basis and Mandate of BMCs under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002
key_dimensions: Section 41 of the BD Act as the enabling provision for BMC constitution
Distinction between 'shall' vs 'may' — whether BMC formation is mandatory or discretionary for local bodies
Role of State Biodiversity Boards in directing local body constitution of BMCs
Comparison with NBA and SBB mandates to identify hierarchical gaps

concepts.name: Composition and Membership Structure of BMCs
key_dimensions: Minimum membership norms and who can be a member (elected vs nominated)
Representation of marginalized groups — women, SC/ST, traditional knowledge holders
Role of the Chairperson and how the chair is elected or appointed
UPSC trap: confusion between composition rules for NBA, SBB, and BMC

concepts.name: Jurisdictional Scope of BMCs — Urban vs Rural Local Bodies
key_dimensions: BMCs in Gram Panchayats vs Municipalities vs Cantonment Boards
Whether BMC jurisdiction follows administrative boundary or ecological boundary
Overlapping jurisdiction issues in biodiversity-rich zones spanning multiple panchayats
Special provisions for Scheduled Areas and 6th Schedule areas under PESA

concepts.name: People's Biodiversity Register (PBR) — Preparation and Legal Status
key_dimensions: BMC's primary statutory duty to prepare and maintain PBRs under Section 41(1)
Content of PBR: comprehensive information on availability and knowledge of local biological resources
Legal evidentiary value of PBR in ABS disputes and benefit-sharing claims
Difference between PBR (local level) and Biodiversity Heritage Site notification (state level)

concepts.name: PBR Methodology and Documentation Process
key_dimensions: Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) tools used in PBR preparation
Role of trained resource persons, NGOs, and academic institutions in facilitation
Language and script challenges in documenting traditional knowledge in PBRs
Quality control and verification mechanisms — SBB oversight role

concepts.name: BMC's Role in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) at Local Level
key_dimensions: BMC's power to levy charges/fees on access to biological resources within its jurisdiction
How BMC interacts with NBA's approval process — consultative vs veto role
Channeling of ABS benefits to local communities through BMCs
Nagoya Protocol implementation at grassroots: BMC as interface institution

concepts.name: Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS) — BMC's Role in Nomination
key_dimensions: Section 37 of BD Act — State Government power to notify BHS on recommendation
BMC's role in identifying and recommending local areas for BHS status
Management responsibilities of BMC post-BHS notification
UPSC trap: BHS notification power lies with State Government, not BMC or NBA

concepts.name: Relationship Between BMC and State Biodiversity Board (SBB)
key_dimensions: SBB's supervisory and capacity-building role over BMCs
SBB's power to issue general orders and guidelines that BMCs must follow
Financial flow: grants and funds routed through SBB to BMCs
Conflict resolution: when BMC decisions conflict with SBB directives

concepts.name: Relationship Between BMC and National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)
key_dimensions: BMC is NOT directly under NBA — indirect relationship via SBB
NBA consultation with BMC in matters of bio-survey and bio-utilization approvals
UPSC trap: NBA deals with foreign nationals/companies; BMC deals with local community-level access
BMC's role in flagging violations to SBB which escalates to NBA

concepts.name: BMC Powers to Regulate Local Access to Biological Resources
key_dimensions: Section 41(2): BMC may levy charges for access to biological resources for commercial purposes
Distinction: Indian citizens need only inform BMC (not seek approval) for non-commercial use
Exemptions: codified traditional uses, cultivated species, and AYUSH practitioners
UPSC trap: local vaids/hakims and farmers are exempt from BMC charges under Section 41

concepts.name: Exemptions and Limitations on BMC Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: Growers and cultivators of biological resources not subject to BMC access charges
Local communities practicing traditional medicine exempt from notification requirement
Scheduled species under Wildlife Protection Act — dual regulatory regime with BMC
Agricultural biodiversity governed separately under PPVFRA — overlap and gap with BMC mandate

concepts.name: Benefit Sharing Fund at Local Level — Local Biodiversity Fund
key_dimensions: Section 43 of BD Act — establishment of Local Biodiversity Fund (LBF) managed by BMC
Sources of LBF: grants from Central/State governments + fees collected by BMC
Utilization of LBF: conservation, sustainable use, and benefit sharing with local communities
UPSC trap: LBF is distinct from NBA's Biodiversity Fund — different level and governance

concepts.name: Traditional Knowledge Protection and IPR Interface at BMC Level
key_dimensions: PBR as a defensive publication tool to prevent bio-piracy and wrongful IPR claims
BMC's role in challenging patent applications based on PBR documentation
Linkage between PBR data and the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL)
Limitations: PBR has no proactive IPR protection — only defensive value

concepts.name: Challenges in BMC Operationalization — Institutional Gaps
key_dimensions: Low awareness among elected representatives of local bodies about BMC duties
Lack of dedicated staff, budget, and technical expertise at BMC level
Inactive BMCs: large number constituted on paper but non-functional in practice
Political economy: resistance from contractors and traders benefiting from unregulated resource extraction

concepts.name: BMCs in Scheduled and Tribal Areas — PESA and Forest Rights Act Interface
key_dimensions: Gram Sabha powers under PESA, 1996 — potential overlap with BMC's biodiversity mandate
Forest Rights Act, 2006: Community Forest Rights (CFR) vs BMC's resource management role
UPSC trap: Gram Sabha under PESA has prior consultation rights on minor forest produce — not BMC
Convergence models: BMC functioning as sub-committee of Gram Sabha in tribal areas

concepts.name: BMC Enforcement Powers and Penalty Provisions
key_dimensions: Whether BMC has direct enforcement or must refer violations to SBB/NBA
Penalty provisions under Chapter X of BD Act applicable to violations at local level
BMC's role as complainant vs adjudicator in biodiversity offence cases
UPSC trap: BMC has no suo motu prosecution power — enforcement flows upward through SBB

concepts.name: Biodiversity Management Committees and Climate Adaptation — Emerging Role
key_dimensions: BMCs as repositories of traditional ecological knowledge relevant to climate resilience
Integration of PBR data into District Disaster Management Plans and Agro-biodiversity mapping
BMC's potential role under National Biodiversity Action Plan (NBAP) 2008 targets
Connection to Aichi Biodiversity Targets and post-2020 Kunming-Montreal GBF at local implementation level

concepts.name: BMC vs Wildlife Protection Act Institutions — Overlapping Mandates
key_dimensions: Eco-Development Committees (EDCs) under Project Tiger vs BMCs — different legislative basis
Van Suraksha Samitis (VSS) under Joint Forest Management vs BMCs — confusion of roles
UPSC trap: EDCs focus on buffer zones of PAs; BMCs cover all local bodies regardless of PA proximity
Convergence or conflict: areas where species under WPA also documented in PBRs

concepts.name: Digital Initiatives and Technology Integration in BMC Functioning
key_dimensions: NBA's e-governance portal for BMC registration and PBR uploading
Geo-tagging of biodiversity resources documented in PBRs
Mobile-based apps (e.g., Biodiversity Register app) for community-driven documentation
Data sovereignty concerns: who owns and controls PBR data uploaded to central databases

concepts.name: BMC Performance Assessment — National Biodiversity Target Monitoring
key_dimensions: Number of BMCs constituted vs functional — a common Prelims data point (over 2.7 lakh constituted by 2023)
PBR completion rates as an indicator of BMC effectiveness in NBAP reviews
5th National Report to CBD — BMC data as part of India's biodiversity target reporting
UPSC trap: constitutional status of BMCs — they are statutory bodies, NOT constitutional bodies
